resolution: Integrated the universal paint kit (runtime/paint) into Studio model-editor paint mode, replacing the bespoke pipeline end-to-end. BrushKit is now the paint panel (tools, brush shapes, size/hardness/flow/scatter/angle dials, blend, the colour wheel, and the saved palette — all as icons, killing the old fixed size-buttons inconsistency), and useBrushStroke is the optimistic host-owned stamping engine, driven by a mapPoint that wraps the existing pickFaceUV → UV-pixel + the hit face's UV-island clip. Everything that worked is preserved: crisp nearest pixels, per-face island clamping (no bleed), the paint undo/redo ring, and content-addressed PNG persistence; the model's saved palette + materials stay the branch source of truth (colour slots become kit swatches, materials a flat-pseudo row, new colours mint back via + save). Studio gains the full tool family it lacked (line/rect/oval/eyedropper, shift-straight lines), plus paint-tool hotkeys (b/e/l/r/o/i) via a new paint-only 'studio-paint' control scope so the kit's native keys don't collide with the mesh-op letters; HotkeysPanel now lists+rebinds both scopes in paint mode. Dropped the dead slot/cell resample machinery the pixel painter made obsolete. Three commits, all build-green (SHIP_RUN_PACKAGE=0 rjit ship hmsc-int) and boot-clean (rjit shot /workbench PASS 372KB). Paint BEHAVIOUR must be live-verified (rjit dev hmsc-int) — paint mode can't be self-shot (object-mode boot only). PaintPanel.tsx is now dead, imported only by the dead Studio.tsx breadcrumb (deletion gated on your word per the handoff).
